about: HAND-ANNOTATED pixel points on the eval images (coordinates in the file as stored in data/eval, i.e. file_size from manifest.json). Read by eye, not detected: each point carries a few px of reading error (px_sd). Points were first read for a throwaway evaluator on 2026-10-28 and copied here unchanged. 'measure' says what the truth is compared with: point_to_point = ground distance between the two points; line_to_line = narrowest distance from the wall-base segment (barrier) to the kerb line (walkway edge). ground_lines are segments along the walkway used to estimate the tilt (vanishing point). Used by scripts/eval_public.py.

items.ground_lines_note: kerb line and wall base: two nearly parallel lines, so the tilt from them is weak

items.points_note: the two ends of the white 1 m folding ruler
items.ground_lines_note: edges of the paved path; ragged grass border, rough

items.points_note: bases of the near ends of the left and right parapets (weak: our assumption of where the 2.30 m is taken)
